content:
Distance can add to the challenges of arthritis and frailty.

This guide covers practical planning. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Transport

  • Community transport schemes.
  • Ask about NHS patient transport if eligible.

Appointments

Ask whether phone or video appointments are possible.

Your rural home

  • Outdoor paths, lighting and steps.
  • Heating and keeping warm.
  • Ask the council for a home assessment.

Staying connected

  • Neighbours and local groups.
  • Phone or video calls.
  • Community alarm services.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I get a care assessment?

Yes, from your council.

What if the weather cuts me off?

Keep spare medicines and supplies.

Sources and further reading

  • GOV.UK: Apply for a needs assessment by social services
  • Community Transport Association
  • NHS: Heatwave: how to cope in hot weather

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
